chapters.title: The LORD Appears to Solomon Again
chapters.html:
1 Kings 9

The Second Appearance

1And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the king's house and all that Solomon desired to do,

2that the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.

3The LORD said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your plea that you made before Me. I have consecrated this house that you have built, by putting My name there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.

4As for you, if you walk before Me as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, doing all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,

5then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised David your father, saying, 'You shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel.'

6But if you or your sons turn back from following Me, and do not keep My commandments and My statutes that I have set before you, but go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

7then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given them, and the house that I have consecrated for My name I will cast out of My sight, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

8As for this house, which is exalted, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

9Then they will say, 'Because they forsook the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them. That is why the LORD has brought all this evil on them.'"

Hiram and the Cities of Galilee

10And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD and the king's house,

11Hiram king of Tyre having supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber and gold, as much as he desired, that King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.

12Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they did not please him.

13He said, "What are these cities that you have given me, my brother?" So they are called the land of Cabul to this day.

14Hiram had sent to the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.

Solomon's Forced Labor and Buildings

15This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon raised to build the house of the LORD and his own house, the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

16(Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and had given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.)

17So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,

18and Baalath and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

19and all the store cities that Solomon had, the cities for his chariots and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.

20All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the sons of Israel —

21their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were not able to devote to destruction — these Solomon raised as forced labor of slaves, to this day.

22But of the sons of Israel Solomon made no slaves. They were the men of war, his servants, his officials, his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

23These were the chief officers who were over Solomon's work, five hundred and fifty, who had charge of the people doing the work.

24But Pharaoh's daughter went up from the City of David to her own house that Solomon had built for her. Then he built the Millo.

25Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built to the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the house.

The Fleet

26King Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.

27Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, seamen who knew the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.

28They went to Ophir and brought from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon… My eyes and My heart will be there" — the first appearance gave gifts (3:5–14); this one answers the prayer of 8:29, that Your eyes may be open toward this house.

  • vv6–7 "if you or your sons turn back… Israel will become a proverb and a byword" — the words of the covenant curses: You will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples (Deuteronomy 28:37).

  • v8 "this house, which is exalted — everyone who passes by it will be appalled" — elyon, high. The Greek has the same, and Chronicles reads this house, which was exalted (2 Chronicles 7:21). Will hiss: sharaq, the whistle of one who sees a ruin.

  • v13 "the land of Cabul" — Cabul is a town on the border of Asher (Joshua 19:27). My brother is how one king addresses another who is bound to him, as Ahab will say of Ben-hadad, He is my brother (20:32). Chronicles tells of cities that Huram had given to Solomon, which Solomon rebuilt and settled (2 Chronicles 8:2).

  • vv15–25 in the Greek — the Greek does not have these verses at this point; its chapter 9 goes from v14 to v26.

  • v16 "had given it as a dowry to his daughter" — shilluchim, parting gifts, the word for what a father sends with a bride.

  • v18 "Tadmor in the wilderness" — the written text has Tamar, the read form Tadmor; the text follows the read form. Chronicles also has Tadmor in the wilderness (2 Chronicles 8:4).

  • vv20–22 "these Solomon raised as forced labor of slaves… But of the sons of Israel Solomon made no slaves" — the Canaanites of Gezer had long been forced labor (Joshua 16:10). The forced labor of Israelites in 5:13–14 was by monthly turns; the text here distinguishes it from slavery.

  • v25 "Three times a year" — the three pilgrim feasts, when all your males shall appear before the face of the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 16:16).

  • vv26, 28 "the Sea of Reeds… four hundred and twenty talents of gold" — Yam Suf, the sea Israel crossed out of Egypt, here its gulf at Eloth. Chronicles has four hundred and fifty talents (2 Chronicles 8:18), and the Greek a hundred and twenty. The text keeps the Hebrew.

then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given them, and the house that I have consecrated for My name I will cast out of My sight, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD and the king's house,

He said, "What are these cities that you have given me, my brother?" So they are called the land of Cabul to this day.
Hiram had sent to the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.

(Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and had given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.)
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

and all the store cities that Solomon had, the cities for his chariots and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the sons of Israel —
their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were not able to devote to destruction — these Solomon raised as forced labor of slaves, to this day.
But of the sons of Israel Solomon made no slaves. They were the men of war, his servants, his officials, his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
These were the chief officers who were over Solomon's work, five hundred and fifty, who had charge of the people doing the work.
But Pharaoh's daughter went up from the City of David to her own house that Solomon had built for her. Then he built the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built to the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the house.
The Fleet
King Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, seamen who knew the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.
They went to Ophir and brought from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

chapters.title: The Queen of Sheba and Solomon's Wealth
chapters.html:
1 Kings 10

The Queen of Sheba

1When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions.

2She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices and very much gold and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she spoke with him of all that was on her heart.

3Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from the king that he did not explain to her.

4When the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,

5the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their clothing, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he offered at the house of the LORD, there was no longer any spirit in her.

6She said to the king, "The report was true that I heard in my own land of your words and of your wisdom,

7but I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes had seen it. Not even the half was told me; your wisdom and prosperity surpass the report that I heard.

8Happy are your men! Happy are these servants of yours, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

9Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! Because the LORD loved Israel forever, He has made you king, to do justice and righteousness."

10Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices come as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

11Moreover, the fleet of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a very great quantity of almug wood and precious stones.

12From the almug wood the king made supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day.

13King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her out of King Solomon's bounty. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her servants.

Solomon's Gold

14The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

15besides what came from the traders and the commerce of the merchants, and from all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.

16King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.

17He made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

18The king also made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with the finest gold.

19The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was rounded at the back. On each side of the seat were armrests, and two lions standing beside the armrests.

20Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on each side. Nothing like it was made in any kingdom.

21All King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None was of silver; silver was not considered as anything in the days of Solomon.

22For the king had a fleet of ships of Tarshish at sea with the fleet of Hiram. Once every three years the fleet of ships of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

23So King Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.

24All the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

25Each of them brought his gift, articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses and mules, so much year by year.

Solomon's Horses and Chariots

26Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

27The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars as plentiful as the sycamore trees of the lowland.

28Solomon's horses were brought from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at a price.

29A chariot could be brought up from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. So too, through them, they were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

Notes

  • v1 "concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions" — le-shem YHWH: the fame of Solomon was bound up with the name of his God. The Greek has the name of Solomon and the name of the LORD. Chidot, riddles, the word of Samson's riddle at his wedding (Judges 14:12).

  • v5 "there was no longer any spirit in her" — ve-lo hayah vah od ruach, the words used of the kings of Canaan when they heard what the LORD had done, there was no longer any spirit in them (Joshua 5:1).

  • v9 "to do justice and righteousness" — mishpat u-tsedaqah, what was said of David, David did justice and righteousness for all his people (2 Samuel 8:15). The foreign queen names the task of the king.

  • vv11–12 "almug wood" — atsei almuggim, known only from this passage. Chronicles spells it algummim (2 Chronicles 9:10), and the Greek has hewn wood. What tree it was is not known.

  • v14 "six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold" — Chronicles gives the same figure (2 Chronicles 9:13).

  • vv16–17 "shields of beaten gold… in the House of the Forest of Lebanon" — these are the shields Shishak king of Egypt will carry away in the days of Rehoboam, all the shields of gold that Solomon had made (14:25–26).

  • v19 "the top of the throne was rounded at the back" — rosh agol, a round top. The Greek has calves' heads, reading egel, calf, for agol, round. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v22 "ships of Tarshish… apes and peacocks" — Tarshish is the far port Jonah sailed for from Joppa (Jonah 1:3); ships of Tarshish are the ships that make such voyages. Tukkiyyim, here peacocks, is found only in this verse and its parallel (2 Chronicles 9:21); what bird or animal it names is uncertain.

  • vv26–29 "Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen… horses were brought from Egypt" — the law of the king: he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses (Deuteronomy 17:16). The same law warns against much silver and gold (17:17) and many wives, and the next chapter opens with his wives.

  • v28 "from Egypt and from Kue" — u-miqveh, read as the name of a land, Kue, and not the common word miqveh, a gathering. The Greek has from Thekoue. Chronicles has miqve both times (2 Chronicles 1:16).

chapters.title: Solomon's Heart Turned Away
chapters.html:
1 Kings 11

Solomon's Wives

1King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite women,

2from the nations of which the LORD had said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not go in among them, and they shall not come in among you, for surely they will turn your hearts away after their gods." Solomon clung to these in love.

3He had seven hundred wives who were princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart away.

4And it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned his heart away after other gods, and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father had been.

5Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the loathsome thing of the Ammonites.

6So Solomon did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and did not follow the LORD fully, as David his father had done.

7Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the loathsome thing of Moab, on the mountain east of Jerusalem, and for Molech the loathsome thing of the sons of Ammon.

8He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.

9The LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice

10and had commanded him concerning this very thing, that he should not go after other gods. But he did not keep what the LORD commanded.

11So the LORD said to Solomon, "Because this has been your way, and you have not kept My covenant and My statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.

12Yet I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.

13However, I will not tear away all the kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of David My servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."

Solomon's Adversaries

14Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he was of the royal seed in Edom.

15For when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, he struck down every male in Edom.

16(For Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.)

17But Hadad fled to Egypt, he and certain Edomites of his father's servants with him, while Hadad was still a little boy.

18They set out from Midian and came to Paran, and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him food and gave him land.

19Hadad found great favor in the eyes of Pharaoh, so that he gave him as his wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

20The sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house. Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.

21When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, so that I may go to my own land."

22Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me, that you are now seeking to go to your own land?" He said, "Nothing; only let me go."

23God also raised up another adversary against him, Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.

24He gathered men around him and became leader of a raiding band, after David killed them. They went to Damascus and lived there, and they made him king in Damascus.

25He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the harm that Hadad did. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.

Jeroboam and Ahijah

26Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow, also lifted up his hand against the king.

27This was the reason he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon was building the Millo and closing up the breach of the City of David his father.

28The man Jeroboam was a man of worth. When Solomon saw that the young man was capable in his work, he put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.

29And it came to pass at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Ahijah had clothed himself with a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open country.

30Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.

31He said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I am about to tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon and give you ten tribes.

32But he shall have one tribe, for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,

33because they have forsaken Me and bowed down to Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab and Milcom the god of the sons of Ammon, and have not walked in My ways, doing what is right in My eyes and keeping My statutes and My judgments, as David his father did.

34Yet I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand; I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David My servant whom I chose, who kept My commandments and My statutes.

35But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and give it to you, ten tribes.

36To his son I will give one tribe, so that David My servant may always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to put My name.

37I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

38And it shall come to pass, if you listen to all that I command you, and walk in My ways and do what is right in My eyes, keeping My statutes and My commandments as David My servant did, that I will be with you and build you a sure house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.

39I will humble the seed of David because of this, but not forever.'"

40Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death, but Jeroboam got up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he stayed in Egypt until the death of Solomon.

The Death of Solomon

41The rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?

42The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

43Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "many foreign women… You shall not go in among them… Solomon clung to these in love" — the law: You shall not intermarry with them… for he will turn your son away from following Me (Deuteronomy 7:3–4), and the law of the king, He shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn aside (Deuteronomy 17:17). Davaq, clung, is the word of a man who clings to his woman (Genesis 2:24).

  • vv4, 6 "his heart was not whole with the LORD… did not follow the LORD fully" — lo hayah levavo shalem, the wholeness Solomon asked of the people: Let your heart therefore be whole with the LORD our God (8:61). Shalem, whole, sounds in Shelomoh.

  • vv5, 7 "Milcom… Molech… the loathsome thing" — shiqquts. The god of the Ammonites is Milcom in v5 and v33, and Molech in v7. The Greek has their king in v7.

  • v11 "I will surely tear the kingdom from you" — qaroa eqra. Samuel said to Saul when his robe tore, The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today (1 Samuel 15:28). The same verb returns in vv30–31, when Ahijah tears his cloak.

  • vv14, 23, 25 "an adversary… another adversary" — satan, three times. Early in the reign Solomon said, there is no adversary (5:4). Hadad's escape to Egypt as a boy follows David's war in Edom (2 Samuel 8:13–14).

  • v28 "a man of worth… the forced labor of the house of Joseph" — gibbor chayil, as Kish is called (1 Samuel 9:1). Sevel, the labor gangs of Ephraim and Manasseh, Jeroboam's own tribes.

  • vv29–30 "a new cloak… tore it into twelve pieces" — salmah chadashah. Salmah, cloak, is written with the same letters as Shelomoh, Solomon (שלמה). The Hebrew says only that he had clothed himself with it; the Greek names Ahijah.

  • vv31–32 "ten pieces… one tribe" — twelve pieces: ten for Jeroboam and one for David's line; the text does not say what becomes of the twelfth. The Greek has two scepters for David's line in v32.

  • v36 "so that David My servant may always have a lamp before Me" — nir, as David's men called him the lamp of Israel (2 Samuel 21:17).

  • v38 "build you a sure house, as I built for David" — bayit ne'eman, the promise to the faithful priest (1 Samuel 2:35) and to David (2 Samuel 7:16), now offered to Jeroboam on condition.

chapters.title: The Kingdom Divided
chapters.html:
1 Kings 12

Rehoboam at Shechem

1Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

2And it came to pass, when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it — for he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — Jeroboam stayed in Egypt.

3They sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

4"Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."

5He said to them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people went away.

6King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel me to answer this people?"

7They spoke to him, saying, "If you will be a servant to this people today and serve them, and answer them and speak good words to them, they will be your servants for all time."

8But he abandoned the counsel that the elders gave him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.

9He said to them, "What do you counsel that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"

10The young men who had grown up with him said to him, "Thus shall you say to this people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us' — thus shall you speak to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.

11And now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"

15So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs from the LORD, so that He might establish His word that the LORD spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

Israel Rebels

16When all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king,
"What share do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
To your tents, Israel!
Now look to your own house, David."
So Israel went to their tents.

17But as for the sons of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

  • v7 "If you will be a servant to this people today… they will be your servants for all time" — eved, the same word both ways: serve them one day, and they will serve you always.

  • v10 "My little finger is thicker than my father's loins" — qotanni, my little one; the word finger is not in the Hebrew, and is supplied from the sense.

  • v15 "for it was a turn of affairs from the LORD" — sibbah; Chronicles has nesibbah (2 Chronicles 10:15). The king's folly serves the word spoken through Ahijah (11:29–39).

  • v16 "What share do we have in David?… To your tents, Israel!" — nearly the cry of Sheba's revolt, We have no share in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel! (2 Samuel 20:1).

  • v18 "Adoram, who was over the forced labor… stoned him to death" — the same office was held by Adoram under David (2 Samuel 20:24) and Adoniram under Solomon (4:6).

  • vv20–21 "except the tribe of Judah alone… the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin" — the one tribe of 11:32, with Benjamin fighting on Judah's side. The Greek adds and Benjamin in v20. After v24 the Greek has a long second account of Jeroboam's rise; the text stays with the Hebrew.

  • vv28, 32–33 "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt… in the month that he had devised from his own heart" — the words of Aaron's calf, These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt (Exodus 32:4). chapters.title: The Man of God from Judah
chapters.html:
1 Kings 13

The Altar at Bethel

1A man of God came out of Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel, while Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

2He cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD and said, "Altar, altar, thus says the LORD: 'A son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name. On you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones shall be burned on you.'"

3He gave a sign the same day, saying, "This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: the altar shall be torn apart, and the ashes that are on it shall be poured out."

4And it came to pass, when the king heard the word that the man of God cried out against the altar in Bethel, that Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" But his hand, which he stretched out against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back to himself.

5The altar also was torn apart, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

6The king answered the man of God, "Entreat the favor of the LORD your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God entreated the favor of the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.

7The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift."

8But the man of God said to the king, "If you give me half your house, I will not go in with you, nor eat bread nor drink water in this place.

9For so I was commanded by the word of the LORD: 'You shall not eat bread nor drink water, nor return by the way that you came.'"

10So he went another way and did not return by the way that he had come to Bethel.

The Old Prophet of Bethel

11Now an old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him all that the man of God had done that day in Bethel; the words that he had spoken to the king, they told to their father.

12Their father said to them, "Which way did he go?" For his sons had seen the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.

13He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.

14He went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak. He said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He said, "I am."

15He said to him, "Come home with me and eat bread."

16He said, "I may not return with you or go in with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water with you in this place,

17for it was said to me by the word of the LORD, 'You shall not eat bread nor drink water there, nor return by the way that you came.'"

18He said to him, "I too am a prophet as you are, and a messenger spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, 'Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He lied to him.

19So he went back with him, and ate bread in his house and drank water.

The Lion on the Road

20And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.

21He cried out to the man of God who came from Judah, "Thus says the LORD: 'Because you have rebelled against the mouth of the LORD and have not kept the command that the LORD your God commanded you,

22but have come back and eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which He said to you, "Eat no bread and drink no water," your body shall not come to the tomb of your fathers.'"

23And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

24He went away, and a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay thrown on the road, with the donkey standing beside it; the lion also stood beside the body.

25Men passed by and saw the body thrown on the road and the lion standing beside the body, and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet lived.

26When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard it, he said, "It is the man of God who rebelled against the mouth of the LORD. The LORD has given him to the lion, which has torn him and killed him, according to the word that the LORD spoke to him."

27He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled it.

28He went and found the body thrown on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the body. The lion had not eaten the body or torn the donkey.

29The prophet took up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey and brought it back, and came to the city of the old prophet to mourn and to bury him.

30He laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, "Alas, my brother!"

31And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.

32For the word that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria shall surely come to pass."

Jeroboam Does Not Turn

33After this Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but again made priests for the high places from among all the people. Whoever wished, he ordained, and he became one of the priests of the high places.

34This thing became the sin of the house of Jeroboam, to cut it off and to destroy it from the face of the earth.

Notes

  • v2 "A son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name" — fulfilled when Josiah burned bones on this altar according to the word of the LORD that the man of God proclaimed (2 Kings 23:16).

  • vv4–6 "his hand… dried up… Entreat the favor of the LORD your God" — va-titbash yado. The hand the king stretched out against the prophet is the one he must ask the prophet to heal. Challeh et penei YHWH, soften the face of the LORD, the phrase of pleading.

  • vv8–9, 16–17 "nor eat bread nor drink water… nor return by the way that you came" — the command is spelled out three times in the chapter, and the man of God repeats it both times he is asked.

  • v11 "His sons came and told him" — the Hebrew has his son came, and then they told; the Greek has his sons came, as vv12–13 and 27 speak of his sons. The text follows the Greek.

  • v18 "a messenger spoke to me by the word of the LORD… He lied to him" — mal'akh, fixed as messenger. The narrator says outright what the man of God could not know.

  • v24 "the lion also stood beside the body" — the lion kills and does not eat, and the donkey stands unharmed (v28). The old prophet reads it as the word fulfilled: according to the word that the LORD spoke to him (v26).

  • v30 "Alas, my brother!" — hoy achi, the mourning cry that Jeremiah says will not be raised for Jehoiakim, They shall not mourn for him, 'Alas, my brother!' (Jeremiah 22:18).

  • vv31–32 "Lay my bones beside his bones" — when Josiah burned the bones of Bethel, he spared the tomb of the man of God, and they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria (2 Kings 23:17–18). The old prophet's request saves his own bones.

  • v32 "the cities of Samaria" — the city of Samaria is not built until Omri's reign (16:24). The phrase names the region by what it became.

  • v33 "Whoever wished, he ordained" — yemalle et yado, he filled his hand, the phrase for installing a priest, as in anoint them and ordain them (Exodus 28:41).

chapters.title: Ahijah's Word against Jeroboam
chapters.html:
1 Kings 14

Jeroboam's Wife Goes to Ahijah

1At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

2Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up, please, and disguise yourself, so that no one will know you are the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, who told me that I would be king over this people.

3Take with you ten loaves, some crumbled cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."

4Jeroboam's wife did so. She got up and went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were fixed because of his age.

5But the LORD had said to Ahijah, "The wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son, for he is sick. Thus and thus you shall say to her." When she came, she was pretending to be another woman.

6When Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you pretend to be another? I am sent to you with hard news.

7Go, tell Jeroboam, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you leader over My people Israel,

8and tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, yet you have not been like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes,

9but you have done evil above all who were before you, and have gone and made for yourself other gods and molten images, provoking Me to anger, and have cast Me behind your back,

10therefore I am about to bring evil on the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, bond or free in Israel, and I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung, until it is all gone.

11Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone who dies in the open country the birds of the heavens shall eat, for the LORD has spoken.'

12As for you, get up, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die.

13All Israel shall mourn for him and bury him, for he alone of Jeroboam's family shall come to a grave, because in him there is found something good toward the LORD, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.

14Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam this day — and what? even now.

15The LORD will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and root up Israel out of this good land that He gave to their fathers, and scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherim, provoking the LORD to anger.

16He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and which he made Israel to sin."

17Then Jeroboam's wife got up and went away and came to Tirzah. As she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.

18They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke by His servant Ahijah the prophet.

19The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred and how he reigned, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

20The time that Jeroboam reigned was twenty-two years. He lay down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

Rehoboam King of Judah

21Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

22Judah did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they provoked Him to jealousy with their sins that they committed, more than all that their fathers had done.

23For they also built for themselves high places, pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

24There were also consecrated men in the land. They did according to all the detestable things of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.

25And it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

26He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took away everything. He also took away all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

27King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and committed them to the hands of the officers of the guard, who kept the door of the king's house.

28As often as the king went into the house of the LORD, the guard carried them and brought them back to the guardroom.

29The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

30There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

31Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. Abijam his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–20 in the Greek — the Greek lacks these verses here; it tells the sickness of Jeroboam's son in its long addition after 12:24.

  • v3 "crumbled cakes" — niqqudim, the word for the Gibeonites' bread, dry and crumbled (Joshua 9:5, 12).

  • v4 "his eyes were fixed because of his age" — qamu einav, the words used of Eli, his eyes were fixed, and he could not see (1 Samuel 4:15). The blind prophet sees through the disguise.

  • v9 "and have cast Me behind your back" — ve-oti hishlakhta acharei gavekha, a figure for contempt, as the LORD says to Jerusalem, you have forgotten Me and cast Me behind your back (Ezekiel 23:35).

  • v10 "every male, bond or free… as one sweeps away dung" — mashtin be-qir, one who urinates against a wall, the idiom of so much as one male (1 Samuel 25:22). Atsur ve-azuv, bond or free, as in there is none left, bond or free (Deuteronomy 32:36). Galal, dung.

  • v14 "this day — and what? even now" — zeh ha-yom u-meh gam attah, a broken phrase whose sense is uncertain. The Greek has no text here to compare.

  • v15 "as a reed is shaken in the water… beyond the River" — beyond the River, the Euphrates. Asherim, the wooden poles of the goddess Asherah.

  • v24 "There were also consecrated men in the land" — qadesh, the word of the law, there shall be no consecrated man among the sons of Israel (Deuteronomy 23:17). The Greek has a conspiracy. Detestable things: to'evot, fixed.

speech.text: 1 Kings 14
Jeroboam's Wife Goes to Ahijah
At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up, please, and disguise yourself, so that no one will know you are the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, who told me that I would be king over this people.
Take with you ten loaves, some crumbled cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did so. She got up and went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were fixed because of his age.
But the LORD had said to Ahijah, "The wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son, for he is sick. Thus and thus you shall say to her." When she came, she was pretending to be another woman.
When Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you pretend to be another? I am sent to you with hard news.
Go, tell Jeroboam, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you leader over My people Israel,

and tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, yet you have not been like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes,
but you have done evil above all who were before you, and have gone and made for yourself other gods and molten images, provoking Me to anger, and have cast Me behind your back,

therefore I am about to bring evil on the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, bond or free in Israel, and I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung, until it is all gone.
Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone who dies in the open country the birds of the heavens shall eat, for the LORD has spoken.'
As for you, get up, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die.

All Israel shall mourn for him and bury him, for he alone of Jeroboam's family shall come to a grave, because in him there is found something good toward the LORD, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam this day — and what? even now.

The LORD will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and root up Israel out of this good land that He gave to their fathers, and scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherim, provoking the LORD to anger.
He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and which he made Israel to sin."
Then Jeroboam's wife got up and went away and came to Tirzah. As she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.
They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke by His servant Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred and how he reigned, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
The time that Jeroboam reigned was twenty-two years. He lay down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam King of Judah

Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they provoked Him to jealousy with their sins that they committed, more than all that their fathers had done.
For they also built for themselves high places, pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
There were also consecrated men in the land. They did according to all the detestable things of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took away everything. He also took away all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and committed them to the hands of the officers of the guard, who kept the door of the king's house.
As often as the king went into the house of the LORD, the guard carried them and brought them back to the guardroom.
The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. Abijam his son reigned in his place.

chapters.title: Abijam, Asa, Nadab and Baasha
chapters.html:
1 Kings 15

Abijam King of Judah

1In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.

2He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

3He walked in all the sins that his father had done before him, and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father had been.

4Nevertheless, for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him and establishing Jerusalem,

5because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and did not turn aside from anything that He commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

6There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

7The rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

8Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Asa his son reigned in his place.

Asa King of Judah

9In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign over Judah.

10He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

11Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his father had done.

12He put away the consecrated men out of the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

13He also removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her horrid image and burned it at the Kidron Valley.

14But the high places were not taken away. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was whole with the LORD all his days.

15He brought into the house of the LORD the things that his father had dedicated and his own dedicated things, silver, gold and vessels.

16There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

17Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

18Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that were left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the treasuries of the king's house, and gave them into the hands of his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

19"Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. I am sending you a present of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."

20Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.

21And it came to pass, when Baasha heard of it, that he stopped building Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.

22Then King Asa made a proclamation to all Judah; none was exempt. They carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building, and with them King Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

23The rest of all the acts of Asa, all his might, all that he did and the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.

24Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father. Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

Nadab King of Israel

25Nadab son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

26He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, with which he made Israel to sin.

27Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him, and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.

28So Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and reigned in his place.

29And it came to pass, as soon as he became king, that he struck down all the house of Jeroboam. He left to Jeroboam not one that breathed, until he had destroyed it, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,

30because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned and that he made Israel to sin, and because of the anger to which he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel.

31The rest of the acts of Nadab and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

32There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

Baasha King of Israel

33In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah began to reign over all Israel at Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.

34He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, with which he made Israel to sin.

Notes

  • vv1, 9 "In the eighteenth year… In the twentieth year of Jeroboam" — from here on the book dates each king by the other kingdom's reign. Abijam begins in Jeroboam's eighteenth year and reigns three years, yet Asa begins in the twentieth, not the twenty-first: the numbers fit only if a part-year at each end counts as a year. Nadab likewise begins in Asa's second year, reigns two years, and dies in Asa's third (vv25, 28).

  • v2 "He reigned three years" — the Greek has six years. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv2, 10 "Maacah daughter of Abishalom" — the same name is given as the mother of Abijam and of his son Asa. In v13 she is removed as gevirah, queen mother, so she held that rank into Asa's reign. Chronicles calls Abijah's mother Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah (2 Chronicles 13:2), and elsewhere Maacah daughter of Absalom (2 Chronicles 11:20). The Greek names Asa's mother Ana.

  • v4 "the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem" — nir, the promise of 11:36.

  • v5 "except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite" — the one exception to David's record that the book names (2 Samuel 11). The Greek lacks the clause.

  • v6 "There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life" — the sentence of 14:30, repeated in the account of Abijam, and v7 adds There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam. The Greek lacks v6.

  • v12 "the consecrated men… all the idols" — qedeshim (14:24) and gillulim, the word of the corpses of your idols (Leviticus 26:30).

  • v13 "a horrid image for Asherah" — mifletset, from the root of shuddering, found only here and in Chronicles' account of the same act (2 Chronicles 15:16).

  • v23 "in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet" — Chronicles adds that in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but the physicians (2 Chronicles 16:12).

  • v29 "He left to Jeroboam not one that breathed" — the word of Ahijah fulfilled: I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung (14:10).

chapters.title: From Baasha to Ahab
chapters.html:
1 Kings 16

Jehu's Word against Baasha

1The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

2"Because I raised you up from the dust and made you leader over My people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have made My people Israel sin, provoking Me to anger with their sins,

3I am about to sweep away Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

4Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country the birds of the heavens shall eat."

5The rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

6Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.

7Moreover, the word of the LORD came by the hand of the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and also because he struck it down.

Elah and Zimri

8In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha began to reign over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned two years.

9His servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspired against him. When he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah,

10Zimri came in and struck him down and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

11And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he struck down all the house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, of his kinsmen or of his friends.

12So Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

13for all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and which they made Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their empty things.

14The rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

15In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. The people were camped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines,

16and the people who were camped there heard it said, "Zimri has conspired, and he has also struck down the king." So all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.

17Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.

18And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the citadel of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire, and he died,

19because of the sins that he sinned, doing evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin that he committed, making Israel to sin.

20The rest of the acts of Zimri and the conspiracy that he carried out, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

Omri

21Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.

22But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.

23In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel, and he reigned twelve years; six years he reigned in Tirzah.

24He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He built on the hill and called the name of the city that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.

25Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did more evil than all who were before him.

26He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins with which he made Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their empty things.

27The rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

28Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his place.

Ahab

29Ahab son of Omri began to reign over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

30Ahab son of Omri did evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.

31As if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as his wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

32He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.

33Ahab also made the Asherah. Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

34In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by Joshua son of Nun.

Notes

  • v2 "Because I raised you up from the dust" — as Hannah sang, He raises the poor from the dust (1 Samuel 2:8), and as the LORD had said to Jeroboam, I raised you up from among the people (14:7).

  • v7 "and also because he struck it down" — Baasha destroyed Jeroboam's house as Ahijah had foretold (15:29), and is judged both for walking in Jeroboam's ways and for the killing. The verse gives both reasons.

  • v9 "drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza" — the king is drunk in his steward's house while the army is at Gibbethon (v15).

  • v11 "a single male, of his kinsmen or of his friends" — mashtin be-qir (14:10). Go'alav, his redeemers, the kinsmen who would have avenged his blood (Numbers 35:19).

  • vv13, 26 "with their empty things" — be-havleihem, hevel, breath, vapor: the idols are nothing. The word of the Song of Moses, they provoked Me with their empty things (Deuteronomy 32:21).

  • vv15–18 "Zimri reigned seven days… burned the king's house over himself" — the shortest reign in the book.

  • vv23, 29 "In the thirty-first year of Asa… twelve years… Ahab… in the thirty-eighth year of Asa" — thirty-one and twelve would pass the thirty-eighth year. The dates fit if Omri's twelve years are counted from his acclamation in the camp in Asa's twenty-seventh year (vv15–16), with part-years counted at each end (27 to 38 is twelve years counted that way), and the thirty-first year marks when he reigned alone, after Tibni died (v22). The Greek calls Omri Zambri and dates Ahab to the second year of Jehoshaphat, on a different reckoning. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v24 "He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer… Samaria" — Shomeron, named after Shemer. From here to the end of the northern kingdom Samaria is its capital; earlier mentions, as in 13:32, use the name it came to have.

  • v31 "Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians" — Etba'al, with Baal. The Sidonian marriage brings the worship of Baal into Israel's capital (vv32–33).

  • v34 "at the cost of Abiram his firstborn… at the cost of Segub his youngest" — the curse Joshua laid on Jericho: At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates (Joshua 6:26). The written text has Segib, the read form Segub.

The rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his place.
Ahab
Ahab son of Omri began to reign over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.

As if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as his wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.
Ahab also made the Asherah. Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by Joshua son of Nun.
